DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Needle Comes Down

STS-HS10-L2-13001400-HSELA910-SOC-GBL-01 • HS English 9-10 • How an Author Unfolds a Series of Ideas
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
A soundtrack is an argument you can hear. Amara, Jiwon, and Tomás are building a four track playlist for an article about a drum rhythm that traveled from West Africa to the Caribbean and then out to the rest of the world. Each track marks one step in how the writer unfolds that story, so track one has to come first for a reason and track four has to land last. Musicians in every country make this choice without ever saying a word about it.
If you moved track four to the front, what would a listener understand differently about the story?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Describe Amara's action in one sentence. Use an exact verb, not "doing something."
2
What is Jiwon holding?
Look at the picture. Describe what Jiwon holds in one sentence. Name the object exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Describe the teacher's action in one sentence. Use an exact verb.
4
What kind of room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Describe this room in one sentence. Name what it is used for.
5
Tell me about the wall behind the students.
Look at the picture. Describe the wall in one sentence. Use an exact noun, not "things."
6
What is Tomás wearing?
Look at the picture. Describe Tomás's clothing in one sentence. Use the exact color and item.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.9-10.3 — Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
